title: The Siege and Judgment of Banu Qurayza
subtitle: Direct March, Fortresses Besieged, and the Verdict of Sa'd ibn Mu'adh
summary: Jibril's instruction in Bukhari 4117, the Asr order in Bukhari 4119, Sa'd ibn Mu'adh's judgment in the wording of Bukhari 4121 and 4122 and Muslim 1769, and the siege details that belong only to the classical sirah.

sections.text: When the Prophet returned from the trench, he laid down his arms and bathed. Aishah reported in Bukhari 4117 that Jibril came and said, 'You have laid down your arms? By Allah, we have not laid them down, so go out to them.' The Prophet asked, 'Where to?' Jibril said, 'Here,' and pointed toward Banu Qurayzah. The classical sirah adds that Jibril arrived on horseback, with dust on him, and said he was going ahead to shake their fortresses. Those extra clauses are not the wording of Bukhari 4117. Both are kept distinct here. A length of a full month for the trench is the sirah's description of the siege, not a figure in this Hadith.

Ibn Umar reported in Bukhari 4119 that the Prophet said, 'None of you should pray Asr except at Banu Qurayzah.' The time of Asr came on the road. Some said they would not pray until they arrived. Others prayed where they were, saying he had meant them to hurry. When this was mentioned to him, he did not blame either group. The report does not say that three thousand men marched.
What the Sirah Adds about the Siege

Bukhari and Muslim describe the march and the judgment. They do not state how many nights the siege lasted, and they do not name the color of a banner, so none is given here. The classical sirah says the siege lasted about twenty-five nights, that Huyayy ibn Akhtab entered the fortresses with Banu Qurayzah, and that Ka'b ibn Asad offered his people three courses: to accept Islam, to fight after killing their own dependents, or to attack on the Sabbath. Those proposals are the biography, not Bukhari 4121.
The Arbitration of Sa'd ibn Mu'adh

Bukhari 4121 says that people had agreed to the judgment of Sa'd ibn Mu'adh and that the Prophet sent for him. The classical sirah places before that an appeal by the Aws. They reminded him that Banu Qurayzah had been their allies, as Banu Qaynuqa' had been allies of another clan, and he then named Sa'd. The appeal is not narrated inside the Bukhari report of the verdict, so it is not told here as if it were that Hadith.

Sa'd had been wounded at the trench. Muslim 1769 says a tent was pitched for him in the mosque and that the wound was in the medial vein of his arm. The classical sirah names Rufaydah al-Aslamiyyah as the woman who tended the wounded in that tent. He was brought on a donkey. The sirah reports that he said the time had come for him not to care about anyone's blame in the cause of Allah. That sentence is the biographical account. It is not a line of Bukhari 4121.

Abu Sa'id reported that the Prophet said, 'Stand up for the best among you,' or 'Stand up for your chief,' and told Sa'd that these people had agreed to his judgment. Sa'd said that their fighting men should be killed and their women and children taken captive. Aishah's report in Bukhari 4122 and Muslim 1769 includes the division of the property as well. The Prophet said, 'You have judged according to Allah's judgment,' or, in the same wording, 'the King's judgment.'

The wording in Bukhari 4121 is 'Allah's judgment,' or 'the King's judgment.' Surah al-Ahzab 33:26–27 speaks of them coming down from their fortresses, of some being killed and some taken captive, and of their land. It does not give a number of the dead, and this chapter does not add one. The account is about Banu Qurayzah and the people named in this siege.

references.title: The Holy Quran
references.author: Surah Al-Ahzab (33:26–27)
references.notes: Divine revelation commemorating the descent of the people of scripture from their fortresses and the division of their lands.

references.title: Sahih al-Bukhari
references.author: Imam Muhammad ibn Isma'il al-Bukhari (d. 256 AH)
references.notes: 4117: Jibril after the arms were laid down, pointing toward Banu Qurayzah. 4119: the Asr instruction and the two groups, neither of them blamed. 4121: 'Allah's judgment' or 'the King's judgment.' 4122: the judgment, Sa'd's supplication, and his death. The old block 4117–4124 is not cited, because not every number in it supports these sentences.

references.title: Sahih Muslim
references.author: Imam Muslim ibn al-Hajjaj (d. 261 AH)
references.notes: Aishah: the wound, the tent in the mosque, the march, and the judgment that the fighters be killed, the women and children taken, and the property divided. The report gives the judgment and the tent in the mosque. It does not add a later scriptural comparison.
